story_title: Add created-date range filtering to GET /api/alerts
story_summary: Add optional inclusive created-date range filters to the alerts list endpoint, reject invalid ranges as 400 validation errors, preserve existing filters/sorting/paging, and cover the change with focused API/service/repository tests.

scope_anchors.reason: Current query contract exposes filters, paging, sorting, and search but no created-date range fields or cross-field range validation.
GET /api/alerts binds AlertQueryRequest from query and already advertises 400 validation behavior under ApiController.
GetAllAsync forwards query options to the repository and must pass through the new date filters.
Repository contract currently stops at existing filters and paging options; it must carry the new range parameters.
Owns the actual alert-list query and currently applies active-status, severity, title-search, sorting, and paging only.

acceptance_criteria: GET /api/alerts accepts optional createdFrom and createdTo query parameters.
createdFrom is inclusive and returns alerts with CreatedDate >= createdFrom.
createdTo is inclusive and returns alerts with CreatedDate <= createdTo.
When both are supplied, both filters are applied together.
When createdFrom is later than createdTo, the API returns 400 Bad Request with a validation error.
Existing filters, sorting, and paging continue to work unchanged.
No database schema or migration changes are required.
Unit tests cover request validation, service pass-through, and repository filtering.
constraints: Preserve the existing controller -> service -> repository layering.
Reuse existing ApiController validation flow where practical.
Do not alter active-status, severity, title-search, sorting, or paging semantics.
No schema, migration, or SQL script changes.
design_decisions: Validate createdFrom <= createdTo at the request boundary so invalid input fails before repository execution.
Apply CreatedDate predicates inclusively in the repository query before count and paging.
Keep controller changes minimal by reusing AlertQueryRequest model binding.
known_facts: The API already supports active-status, severity, title search, sorting, and paging filters.
AlertQueryRequest currently does not expose created-date filters.
AlertsController GET /api/alerts already binds AlertQueryRequest from query and advertises 400 responses.
AlertManagementService currently forwards query options to the repository.
AlertRepository currently applies status, severity, search, sorting, counting, and paging but no created-date predicates.
No database schema or migration changes are required.
